1.title: Pull out the house wires
1.say: Pull the two white wires and two black wires out of the gray box in the wall. Leave the bare copper tips pointing straight out in front.
placements: two white house wires with bare copper tips → pulled forward out of the gray wall box to hang in front of the opening in the video: center right of the white wall
two black house wires with bare copper tips → pulled forward out of the gray wall box to hang in front of the opening in the video: center right of the white wall
watch_for: If you see only two wires, the other two are still folded inside so reach in and pull them forward.
If one bare copper tip touches another bare tip, you can get a short so keep all four ends apart.
1.check_yourself: It should look like four bare copper tips sticking straight out of the gray box with no caps on.
1.safety: Switch the power off at the breaker before you touch any wire.

2.title: Check the wires have no power
2.say: Hold the yellow tester in one hand. Touch the red and black tips to each bare copper end in the box.
placements: yellow hand tester with red tip and black tip → both tips touched to each bare copper wire end sticking out of the gray wall box in the video: at the lower edge of the box opening
watch_for: If the tester lights up or beeps, power is still on so stop and switch the breaker off.
If you test only one wire, you can miss power so touch the tips to every bare end.
2.check_yourself: It should look like the yellow tester tips touching the bare wires with no light and no beep.
2.safety: Keep your fingers on the plastic handles only and keep the bare ends apart.

3.title: Join the white wires together
3.say: Twist the two white house wires together inside the gray box. Screw the small yellow cap tightly over the bare copper ends. Push the capped white wires to the back of the gray box.
placements: two white house wires with bare copper ends → twisted together clockwise until tight and tucked to the back inside the gray wall box in the video: back left inside the box
small yellow twist cap → screwed tightly over the twisted white wire ends inside the gray wall box in the video: back left inside the box
watch_for: If copper shows below the yellow cap, unscrew it and twist tighter until no copper shows.
If a white and black wire are twisted together, undo it and keep white only with white.
3.check_yourself: It should look like the two white wires hidden under a yellow cap pushed to the back with only two black wires sticking out.
3.safety: Keep the breaker off while you twist the white wires together.

4.title: Connect first black wire to thermostat
4.say: Hold one black house wire next to one short black wire from the thermostat box. Twist the bare copper ends together in front of the gray box. Screw the big red cap over the bare ends.
placements: one black house wire with bare copper end → twisted clockwise to one short black wire hanging from the black thermostat box in front of the gray wall box in the video: left side of the opening
one short black wire hanging from the black thermostat box with white knob → twisted clockwise to the one black house wire in front of the gray wall box in the video: left side of the opening
big red twist cap → screwed tightly over the joined bare ends in front of the gray wall box in the video: left side of the opening
watch_for: If copper shows below the red cap, the joint is loose so unscrew and twist tighter.
If you grab the free black house wire by mistake, you will have no wire left for the other side so work with one only.
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black house wire joined under a red cap to the hanging black box with the other black house wire still free.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off while you join the wires because they can carry power.

5.title: Connect the second black wire
5.say: Hold the free black house wire next to the hanging short black wire. Twist the bare copper ends together in front of the gray box. Screw another big red cap over the bare ends.
placements: free black house wire with bare copper end → twisted clockwise to the hanging short black wire from the black thermostat box in front of the gray wall box in the video: right side of the opening
hanging short black wire from the black thermostat box with white knob → twisted clockwise to the free black house wire in front of the gray wall box in the video: right side of the opening
another big red twist cap → screwed tightly over the joined bare ends in front of the gray wall box in the video: near the center of the opening
watch_for: If copper shows below the red cap, the joint will overheat so twist tighter until hidden.
If both house wires end up in one cap, the heater will not switch so keep one house wire per cap.
5.check_yourself: It should look like both black house wires joined to the hanging black box with no bare copper showing.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off while you join the second wires together.

6.title: Screw the thermostat to wall
6.say: Tuck all the capped wires gently into the gray box. Hold the black box with the white knob flat over the wall opening. Drive the top and bottom silver screws into the gray box with a drill.
placements: black thermostat box with white knob → held flat and centered over the gray wall box opening covering the capped wires in the video: centered on the white wall
top silver screw → driven through the top hole of the black box into the top hole of the gray wall box with a power drill in the video: top center of the black box
bottom silver screw → driven through the bottom hole of the black box into the bottom hole of the gray wall box with a power drill in the video: bottom center of the black box
watch_for: If the black box rocks or gaps, a wire is trapped behind so push the wires deeper and reseat flat.
If a screw spins without biting, it missed the hole so back out and line up with the gray box holes.
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black box with the white knob screwed flat and centered over the wall opening.
6.safety: Keep the breaker off while you tuck the wires and drive the screws.

7.title: Push on the white cover
7.say: Line up the white square cover over the black box. Push it straight in until it clicks.
placements: white square plastic cover with round dial → pushed straight onto the black thermostat box centered on the white wall in the video: centered on the white wall
watch_for: If the cover gaps on one side, it is crooked so pull off and line up square before pushing.
If the round dial will not turn, the cover is pressed on the knob wrong so lift and reseat straight.
7.check_yourself: It should look like a white square cover with a round dial centered flat on the white wall.
